record.paper_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Under exactly what physical, angular, and surface-design conditions are RIS-induced channels reciprocal or non-reciprocal, and what validated theory or experimental evidence is needed to support communication-system models that assume a non-reciprocal RIS?

evidence.quote: A resolution of the differences between these results, and a conclusive determination of the conditions under which RIS-induced channels are reciprocal or non-reciprocal, will be welcomed. The system model and applications for a non-reciprocal RIS may be of interest in future applications, but is in need of verifiable theory and/or experimental evidence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is a planar array of N sub-wavelength scattering elements, each of which can be configured to impose a controllable complex reflection coefficient on an incident electromagnetic wave. Let an incident plane wave arrive at the surface from direction (θ_i, φ_i) with polarization p_i, and let the scattered field be observed in direction (θ_r, φ_r) with polarization p_r. Model the RIS as a linear two-port (or multi-port) device with a scattering operator S(θ_i, φ_i, p_i; θ_r, φ_r, p_r; Φ), where Φ = diag(e^{jϕ_1}, …, e^{jϕ_N}) encodes the per-element configuration, possibly augmented by lumped passive/active loads, magnetic biasing, or time-modulated impedances.

The RIS-induced channel is said to be reciprocal if, for every configuration Φ and every pair of directions/polarizations,
   S(θ_i, φ_i, p_i; θ_r, φ_r, p_r; Φ) = S(θ_r, φ_r, p_r; θ_i, φ_i, p_i; Φ),
and non-reciprocal otherwise.

Problem. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on
 (a) the physical realization of the unit cells (material constitutive relations, presence of magneto-optical, time-varying, or nonlinear components, active circuitry),
 (b) the angular geometry of incidence and reflection (including specular versus anomalous reflection regimes and near-field versus far-field operation), and
 (c) the surface design parameters (element spacing relative to wavelength, mutual coupling, load termination network, configuration Φ),
under which the scattering operator S satisfies the reciprocity identity above. Furthermore, for cases in which the identity fails, formulate a rigorously derived communication-channel model H_{RIS}(Φ) for a non-reciprocal RIS that is consistent with Maxwell's equations and energy-conservation constraints, and identify the experimentally measurable quantities that would distinguish reciprocal from non-reciprocal regimes.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on reconfigurable intelligent surfaces continues to debate the conditions for channel reciprocity. Standard passive, linear, time-invariant, isotropic RIS designs are generally argued to be reciprocal by Lorentz reciprocity, but anomalous-reflection metasurfaces, space-time-modulated, magnetically biased, or actively loaded RIS designs have been proposed as non-reciprocal, with conflicting modeling assumptions in the communications literature. As of 2026 no consensus theorem or definitive experimental validation has settled the necessary and sufficient conditions, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Non-reciprocal metasurfaces overview
status_evidence.snippet: Resolution of the differences between these results, and a conclusive determination of the conditions under which RIS-induced channels are reciprocal or non-reciprocal, will be welcomed.
status_evidence.claim: The reciprocity conditions for RIS-induced channels remain unresolved and a communication model for non-reciprocal RIS still lacks verifiable theory and/or experimental evidence.
